scope: All six included decisions for five judges; 71 pages read in full, including concurrences and limitations.
method: Read full cached primary opinion texts, then independently re-extracted all six PDFs with PyMuPDF and confirmed normalized text equality and original ledger SHA-256 matches. Checked captions, reviewing dates, actual judicial actions and reasoning, disposition and precise evidentiary pinpoints against every summary.
result: All six summaries supported; no material correction required.

cases.verified: Caption identifies Goldish; paragraphs 4-5 report the February 21, 2024 refusal to review continuing detention and jurisdiction rationale. Paragraphs 18-27 establish retained circuit jurisdiction and distinct continuing review duty. Paragraphs 29-30 reverse and remand, not release. Initial detention affirmance was a separate appeal.

Caption identifies Goldish; paragraph 18 reports unavailability, reliability and corroboration findings and one-year plenary order. Paragraphs 21-32 affirm the evidentiary determination under abuse-of-discretion review, and paragraph 33 affirms. The order protects the petitioner and three children; it is not a criminal conviction.

Caption identifies Hansen. Paragraphs 14-19 distinguish her grant of postconviction relief from later refusal of a certificate of innocence. Paragraphs 25-27 narrow and modify the certified legal question. Paragraphs 31-39 require a certificate when specified prerequisites are met, without an additional affirmative innocence finding; paragraphs 41-42 answer and remand. No 1998 trial action is attributed to Hansen. Special concurrence also read.

Caption identifies Kuzas. Paragraph 7 reports constructive-possession findings and 30-day time-served sentence; it expressly says he did not mention the CCL statements. Supreme Court paragraphs 28-32 affirm based on no independent corroboration requirement for the license admission. Neville/Rochford and OBrien special concurrences were read and remain distinct from Kuzas reasoning. Cover confirms rehearing denial November 25, 2024.

Caption identifies Martinez. Paragraphs 34-38 report abuse findings, further mental-health evaluation, supervised video visits and equal GAL fees. Paragraphs 82-99 preserve the fact that she rejected ending all parent-child contact. Paragraphs 100 and 110-111 vacate only the supervision arrangement and fee allocation for rehearing; same result remains possible. Other conditions and protection order affirmed.

Caption identifies McGuire. Paragraphs 8-12 and 19 support removal, refusal to vacate and successor appointment. Paragraphs 34-38 acknowledge incomplete transcripts and affirm on available evidence; the ledger preserves that limitation. Paragraphs 40-41 decline contempt review because no notice was filed, rather than affirming contempt merits. Rule 23 notice confirmed.

limitations: This review verifies the cited decision texts and their recorded historical outcomes, not a comprehensive citator or later trial-docket search. The ledgers already disclose unverified subsequent proceedings.
Official index publication-status labels were not freshly queried in this second-reader pass; publication/caption details were checked in the actual documents.
No personal partisan inference or Trumpism score is supported by these case-specific records.
optionalEditorialNote: In Rivera, review continued detention is marginally clearer than reconsider continued detention because paragraph 26 expressly distinguishes statutory continuing review from reconsideration of the initial order; the current summary does not actually conflate them.
